nodes.label: AI Swarm Dynamics Hackathon
nodes.rationale: Hosted by AI Village (The AI Digest) x Grove Research on a custom site with an Airtable form - not Devpost, Devfolio or MLH, so there is no gallery, no public voting and no star-rating rubric. $3,000 across the top five projects, no tracks, no mandated sponsor technology. Theme verbatim: 'Building the tools we wished we had for the Hugging Face incident'.

nodes.label: Constraint: Solo Builder
nodes.rationale: Team is SOLO (confirmed by the user 2026-10-02). Everyone registers solo and teams form after registration, but being online removes Saturday-morning teammate recruiting. Consequence carried into feasibility: one user, one workflow, one before-and-after, and an explicit out-of-scope list.

nodes.label: Constraint: Online Attendance
nodes.rationale: Attendance is ONLINE. No live demo slot (the 18:00-19:00 PT demos are in-person, livestreamed), no teammate recruiting, and the write-up plus video plus public repo carry the entire submission because a judge may never run the code.

nodes.label: Constraint: ~20 Working Hours
nodes.rationale: Build window Sat 2026-10-03 10:00 PT to Sun 2026-10-04 17:00 PT - about 31 hours elapsed and roughly 20 working hours. Pre-work is explicitly permitted ('Feel free to get started early!') but the user has none available, so the schedule is set by what is outside the builder's control.

nodes.label: Constraint: No Compute Reimbursement
nodes.rationale: The $200 compute reimbursement and the Anthropic credits are in-person only, so inference is paid by the builder. An LLM pass over 1.14M computer-use turns is financially out of reach, which is why a cheap deterministic pre-filter is the only affordable shape - and that is also what survives the wrapper filter.

nodes.label: Constraint: No Published Judging Criteria
nodes.rationale: No rubric or weights are published. Home page: '~3-5 judges (members of the AI Village staff and experts in the field)'; logistics page: 'A panel of Grove Research and AI Village staff will review submissions', decisions roughly a week later. Every criterion is therefore marked `assumed`, and with no gallery, voting or rating UI the write-up must say what it wants credited.

nodes.label: Constraint: Submission = Write-up + Repo + Optional Results
nodes.rationale: Submission is a short write-up or video, a public GitHub repo, and optionally a write-up of real results found using the tool, plus team names and emails. The optional results write-up is treated as mandatory because the panel is research staff at two research orgs, one of which has said publicly that unprocessed data is its binding constraint.

nodes.label: Assumed Judging Criteria Table
nodes.rationale: Execution quality and methodological soundness ~30%; impact on the investigators' real workflow ~25%; real results on real data ~20%; originality and prior art ~15%; presentation and clarity ~10%; theme fit as a gate rather than a weight. Every row is marked `assumed` because no rubric exists.

nodes.label: Canary Maze
nodes.rationale: SURVIVOR. A site issues every automated visitor its own secret - a canary URL and a fact-token minted as HMAC(path, fingerprint, salt) - and records which other context later asks for it. Rationale for the mechanism: detection asks 'do these look alike?', which is what the 11 existing CIB tools do and what is failing as agents learn to look like browsers; planting asks 'did they talk?'. Kept over Swarm Ledger because the do-not-fork competitor bucket came back empty. Hard part is the serving layer, not the ledger: a secret issued to context A must still return 200 for B, so the weekend goes to DNS.

nodes.label: Batch Card
nodes.rationale: SURVIVOR. One collapsed card - 'submission 14 of 112 opened by 9 accounts in 6h across 40 repos' - and never a word about who wrote it. Rationale: the quality of one submission is arguable, the shape of the batch is not, and refusing to judge authorship is deliberate because authorship is the claim a maintainer cannot act on socially. A batch is asserted only when >=N members share a deterministic key; model-only matches render as 'possible' and never count toward N. The GitHub App was cut because a third-party App sees only installed repos, so on a solo weekend there is no 'cross'.

nodes.label: Deterministic Core Principle
nodes.rationale: Every survivor is deliberately built so a deterministic core carries the result: membership, existence or a signature is recomputed from stored keys and a model can never cause an assertion on its own. Rationale: inference is unfunded for an online builder with no compute reimbursement, and a deterministic core is simultaneously what survives the wrapper filter and what a judge can test by switching the model off.

nodes.label: Wrapper Filter (Stage 4b/6W)
nodes.rationale: Product first, AI second. For each solution: state what the product is with no model named, where AI creates leverage, and what survives if the model disappeared (substantial / thin / nothing). A solution whose pre-registered reduction sentence is a fair summary dies. Eight wrapper-smell questions plus a declared wrapper shape. This filter killed 'Ask the log' and the 'Swarm brief / question battery'.

nodes.label: Sponsor Verdict: No Sponsor Fit
nodes.rationale: AI Village supplies framing and a 177 GB gated corpus, not an API; Grove Research supplies no API, SDK or dataset and is relevant only as published interests on the panel; Anthropic's $200 reimbursement is in-person only. None of the survivors analyses agent transcripts, which is a direct consequence of the builder being online with no compute reimbursement.

nodes.label: Tooling Fingerprint Join
nodes.rationale: stage: wrapper (regenerated from the citation kill, then killed on four independent grounds measured against the organizers' own three dump files). Reason: 'The premise is factually false: the shared proxy URLs are the same literal string, copied - https://md.succ.ai/https://www.sec.gov/files/county.json appears under 198 distinct accounts and the r.jina.ai equivalent under 147. 198 agents did not independently configure a proxy and independently prefix that exact SEC path with it; they read it off a wiki page and pasted it.' The groups are explained by copying, not by tooling; the key is low-entropy; the trivial join already recovers the group; and the incident report already names the tooling.

nodes.label: Non-existent Source Sweep
nodes.rationale: stage: critic. Reason, verbatim: 'KILLED by measurement on the organizers' own dump, not by argument: running the idea's own extractors over all 14,591 revisions of revisions.jsonl.gz returned 0 DOIs, 0 ISBNs and 0 ref-or-cite templates, so three of its four extractors have no input at all.' Of the 69% of revisions carrying a bare URL, 8,473 URLs are shared by two or more accounts and the top hosts are wikiservice.at, jqp.vercel.app, api.datausa.io and markdown-scraping proxies - shared tooling, not shared sources.

nodes.label: Ask the Log
nodes.rationale: stage: wrapper. Reason, verbatim: 'Feed the access log to a model and print the explanation. The reduction sentence - the user gives their access log to a model and gets an explanation back - is a fair summary, and nothing survives the model: no stable identity, no rules produced, nothing persisted, no claim re-checkable. Regenerated into the two site-operator solutions.'

nodes.label: Swarm Brief / Standard Question Battery
nodes.rationale: stage: wrapper. Reason: 'Point it at a corpus, run ~20 pre-written questions, get a brief. Fuses three organizer suggestions, and its reduction sentence - the user gives 170k agent transcripts to a model and gets a brief back - is verbatim the one pre-registered in defaults.md before any research. Owns no provenance, no record, no action and no check.' A hash-chained re-runnable case file would have survived but was out of reach for a solo 20-hour build, so audience group G9 was dropped and reported as a gap rather than patched.

nodes.label: Swarm Ledger
nodes.rationale: stage: competition. Reason: 'Killed on the competitor scan, not on evidence: the mechanism is claimed by PayPal US12034731B2 (grouping log entries and assigning a corresponding common actor identifier, persisting over 12 months), marketed commercially by WebDecoy (JA4 as a correlation key inside a persistent actor identity), and already stubbed in a public repo. Its own core claim that nobody answers whether requests are one actor is falsifiable in one search.' Separately, the only real recent CC-BY access-log release pseudonymises IPs and user-agents, so the decisive join keys cannot be demonstrated on real public data.

nodes.label: Cohort Console
nodes.rationale: stage: shortlist. Reason: 'Strong product, wrong event: its evidence is 2024-dated and the problem predates the agent era by the discovery pass's own account, why_now.kind is none, and a signup-spam wave is not demonstrably a coordinated AI agent swarm, so it risks reading off-theme.'

nodes.label: Participation Receipts
nodes.rationale: stage: shortlist. Reason: 'The market rests on a single opened evidence item, so the problem is a hypothesis. Retained inside the canary idea's demo plan as a venue rather than shown as its own idea.'

nodes.label: Reciprocal Evidence Exchange
nodes.rationale: stage: shortlist. Reason: 'Judged thin at the wrapper filter: a dependent second surface with nothing to publish without the batch index upstream. Retained as that idea's expansion path.' Classic two-sided first-supply problem.

nodes.label: Fabrication Registry
nodes.rationale: stage: shortlist. Reason: 'Thin for the same reason: without the sweep upstream nothing fills it. Retained as that idea's expansion path.'

nodes.label: Platform Trust-and-Safety Actor Clustering
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'Eleven open safety and security engineering roles at one employer is spend, but a single organisation, and no first-person account from this segment could be opened. The field is also the best-funded one adjacent to the theme and these teams build in-house.' Indeed and Upwork both returned 403, so the second employer signal was unreachable.

nodes.label: Debugging Your Own Multi-Agent System
nodes.rationale: stage: prior-art. Reason: 'Genuinely good evidence - three engineers describing the pain in their own words - but the market answered in 2026. A repo search for multi-agent observability created since 2026-01-01 returns open-multi-agent at 6,972 stars with durable approvals and verifiable run records, plus four more above 400 stars. Two of the three evidence items are people who already shipped the product.'

nodes.label: Alert Fatigue at Swarm Scale
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'One opened comment speaking only for its author, sitting inside the already-crowded multi-agent observability field. Not worth a second lookup against that prior art.'

nodes.label: Package-Registry Abuse-Report Triage
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'Registry staff's own words describe free-form email reporting that scales poorly, but the two best items date from 2022-11 and 2018-02, far outside the 24-month window, and there was no budget to check whether the reporting API they proposed has since shipped. Killed rather than guessed.'

nodes.label: EU AI Act Article 50 Marking Duties
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'A rule proves an obligation, not pain. Retained as a forced-change why-now contribution to the wiki and community-moderation problems rather than kept as a problem of its own, which also held rules-and-deadlines to one twelfth of the pool.'

nodes.label: The Two-Tier Agent-Identity World
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'Cloudflare signed agents went GA 2025-08-28 covering five named agents, while the Web Bot Auth architecture draft expired and was replaced. This is the enabling change behind the site-operator problem, not a separate user problem, so it was folded in as a why-now including the honest read that the protocol is still in flux.'

nodes.label: Small-Forum Admin Signup Waves
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'Real, consumer-adjacent and non-US, but the same job as the community-moderation problem at a tenth of the volume. Merged into it as the low-end segment rather than counted twice; its value was proving the cohort-action job exists on a second unrelated platform.'

nodes.label: Duke Canary Token Paper (arXiv 2605.13706)
nodes.rationale: Closest prior art to Canary Maze and the one to cite first rather than be caught by: 'We host dynamic websites that serve unique canary tokens to each visiting scraper' and 'we maintain a mapping between scrapers and the tokens served to them'. It identifies clients by User-Agent and ASN and verifies by prompting 22 model products after waiting two months, establishing scraper-to-model ingestion. What is left for Canary Maze is the sighting channel, not the minting.

nodes.label: Canarytokens (Thinkst)
nodes.rationale: The incumbent honeytoken primitive - 'motion sensors for your networks, computers and clouds' - one token per asset, generated by a human in a form. The guide page opened describes no per-visitor generation, no cross-client tracking and no graph.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Stealth Crawler Investigation (2025-08-04)
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare created brand-new unindexed domains with a restrictive robots.txt and queried a model about them, then observed '3-6m daily requests' from a stealth crawler behind a desktop Chrome user-agent rotating 'different ASNs in attempts to further evade website blocks'. It independently demonstrates the failure mode Canary Maze addresses - the identifiers a client presents are under the client's control - but the published post contains no records a reader can check.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Web Bot Auth / Signed Agents
nodes.rationale: Signed agents went GA 2025-08-28, verifying a five-agent allowlist by HTTP message signature. Cloudflare's own documentation states the limit: 'Verification proves operator identity only. It is not authorization, not intent, and not a decision about whether the request is welcome.' The declared tier is solved; the undeclared tier has no attribution primitive.

nodes.label: Pyison (MIT, 125 stars)
nodes.rationale: Forkable plumbing for Canary Maze's maze and serving layer - about 60% of the serving work and none of the mechanism. Applies the rule 'fork the plumbing, own the mechanism': everything judged stays the builder's own.

nodes.label: GitHub Pull Request Cap
nodes.rationale: The platform owner wrote the gap down: GitHub's own post says the cap 'does nothing when someone opens pull requests across hundreds of repositories at once', with cross-repository controls still only being explored. The cap is per contributor per repository, so nine accounts across forty repos stay fully compliant - up to 1,080 compliant submissions.

nodes.label: open-slop GitHub Action
nodes.rationale: Owns the per-author burst signal but holds one account at a time, so it can never say 'nine accounts'. The nearest existing alternative to Batch Card on the per-author axis.

nodes.label: Wiz prt-scan Campaign Report
nodes.rationale: 'Six accounts, one actor': a security vendor needed three weeks to establish that six accounts opening 500+ pull requests were one actor. Batch Card computes the same three signals at triage time rather than three weeks later, and the report is the independent published account the replay is checked against. About 95% of the documented campaign came from one account, leaving a ~25-submission multi-account tail that barely exercises the mechanism.

nodes.label: Socket (unchecked competitive risk)
nodes.rationale: Socket published the reputation-farming research and holds cross-ecosystem data, so whether it already ships a maintainer-facing batch view is the biggest unchecked competitive risk for Batch Card. Its product pages were never opened - declared as a research gap.

nodes.label: Survey of 281 Written AI Policies
nodes.rationale: Academic survey supporting Batch Card's social constraint: roughly one in five written policies tells a volunteer to ban the user, and label adoption sits at 2.1% - which is why the card states a shape and names nobody.

hyperedges.label: Wrapper filter kills: the pre-registered reduction sentence firing on three ideas
Solo + online + ~20h + no compute forces a deterministic core
